title: Build a 5-year three-statement forecast for Northline Precision
skills_assessed: Working capital, CapEx, and D&A rollforwards

role.title: Financial analyst
role.company_context: Mid-size US light manufacturer (industrial fasteners / OEM precision hardware). FP&A partners with operations and finance leadership on the annual operating plan, monthly closes, and scenario forecasts. Hiring an analyst who can own an integrated three-statement model without turning the exercise into valuation theater.
day_to_day: Maintain linked income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow models for planning cycles
Translate volume, margin, CapEx, and working-capital drivers into annual forecasts
Reconcile forecast outputs to historical trends and flag integration breaks
Summarize cash, leverage, and earnings implications for FP&A leadership
Document assumptions and sensitivities in plain language
required_skills: Can build or rebuild an integrated three-statement model in a spreadsheet
Comfortable with manufacturing drivers: revenue growth, gross margin, opex, D&A, CapEx, and NWC days
Can verify BS balance, RE rollforward, and cash bridge
Can explain assumptions and at least one material sensitivity
nice_to_have_skills: Prior FP&A or corporate finance experience in manufacturing or industrials
Familiarity with LibreOffice Calc or Excel best practices (separate drivers, checks)
Exposure to debt schedules and simple covenant / liquidity framing
constraints: Assessment is a spreadsheet forecasting work sample — not valuation, coding, or ERP implementation
Candidates may use LibreOffice, Excel, calculator, and browser research for definitions only
Starter CSVs and drivers on the desktop are shared scenery, not a solved forecast
Do not require paid data terminals or company-specific filings beyond the desktop pack

problem_statement.title: Build a 5-year three-statement forecast for Northline Precision
problem_statement.summary: You are the financial analyst supporting FP&A at Northline Precision Components, a mid-size US light manufacturer of industrial fasteners and OEM precision hardware. Leadership wants an integrated three-statement model for the annual operating plan under the base growth case (moderating growth after a strong FY2024, gradual gross-margin improvement, and CapEx that stays elevated early then normalizes). Starter files on the desktop give three years of history (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow), forecast drivers, and a blank model checklist — use them.
outcomes: Rebuild / link the historical statements enough to confirm they integrate (BS balances, RE rollforward, cash bridge).
Produce a 5-year annual forecast (FY2025–FY2029) for the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement using the provided drivers.
Report key outputs: Y5 revenue, Y5 net income, Y5 ending cash, cumulative 5-year free cash flow (CFO + CFI), and Y5 net cash (cash − debt).
Document assumptions and call out at least one material sensitivity or risk.
constraints: Stay inside the provided company, history, and driver set unless you explicitly label a side case.
Do not build a DCF, comps, or valuation memo — this is a three-statement forecast work sample.
Prefer a spreadsheet (LibreOffice Calc / Excel) a reviewer can open; short written notes are fine alongside.
Talk through your reasoning; opaque scrap numbers without links or checks are weak.
problem_statement.deliverables: An auditable workbook (and/or completed model_template.md) with linked IS / BS / CF for history checks and the 5-year forecast, plus brief assumption notes. Optional charts are fine; not required.

rubric.name: Statement integration
rubric.description: YES/NO: Does the deliverable show an integrated model where the balance sheet balances each forecast year, retained earnings roll forward from net income (less dividends), and ending cash ties to the cash flow bridge? Answer YES only if these integration checks are visible for the forecast (history checks strengthen but do not replace forecast integration). Broken BS, orphan NI, or cash that does not bridge = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Forecast driver application
rubric.description: YES/NO: Are revenue growth, gross margin, opex (ex-D&A), tax rate, CapEx (% of sales), and the stated D&A policy applied consistently with forecast_drivers.txt for the instance? Answer YES only if the forecast path clearly follows those drivers rather than freehand fiction. Ignoring drivers or inventing a different primary case without labeling it = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Working capital and manufacturing realism
rubric.description: YES/NO: Are AR, inventory, and AP (or equivalent NWC) set from the stated DSO/DIO/DPO days, and is net PP&E rolled with CapEx − D&A? Answer YES only if both NWC days and the PP&E rollforward are present and coherent. Flat WC with no policy, or CapEx/D&A that never touch PP&E = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Assumptions and sensitivity
rubric.description: YES/NO: Does the candidate document key assumptions and call out at least one material risk or sensitivity (growth, margin, CapEx, WC days, or similar)? Answer YES only if both documentation and a concrete sensitivity/risk note are present. Numbers with no commentary, or generic caveats with no model link = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Clarity of deliverable
rubric.description: YES/NO: Is there an auditable workbook or completed template a reviewer can follow without guessing units, years, or which driver set was used? Answer YES if the path from drivers to outputs is reviewable. Opaque scrap tabs or missing finals that force guessing = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

invariants: Keep the same skills_assessed and rubric structure/weights
Keep the same deliverable kinds and difficulty band (integrated 5-year three-statement manufacturing forecast from provided history + drivers)
Keep US light-manufacturing FP&A framing — not valuation, coding, or a different industry
Keep isomorphic difficulty via CapEx as % of sales, shared D&A rate, and company scales in a similar revenue band
Do not turn the challenge into a DCF, comps exercise, or ERP/software build

values.product_line: industrial fasteners and OEM precision hardware
sheet-metal assemblies and welded OEM enclosures

values.scenario_blurb: moderating growth after a strong FY2024, gradual gross-margin improvement, and CapEx that stays elevated early then normalizes
an approved near-term capacity and tooling program: higher early CapEx, slightly faster volume growth, and gradual margin expansion as utilization improves
a softer demand backdrop: slower growth, slightly tighter margins and higher opex ratio, deferred CapEx, and longer inventory/receivable days

apply.candidate_brief:
## Build a 5-year three-statement forecast for {{company_name}}

You are the financial analyst supporting FP&A at {{company_name}}, a mid-size US light manufacturer of {{product_line}}. Leadership wants an integrated three-statement model for the annual operating plan under the **{{scenario_name}}** case ({{scenario_blurb}}). Starter files on the desktop give three years of history (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow), forecast drivers, and a blank model checklist — use them.

### Outcomes
- Rebuild / link the historical statements enough to confirm they integrate (BS balances, RE rollforward, cash bridge).
- Produce a **5-year annual** forecast (FY2025–FY2029) for the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement using the provided drivers.
- Report key outputs: Y5 revenue, Y5 net income, Y5 ending cash, cumulative 5-year free cash flow (CFO + CFI), and Y5 net cash (cash − debt).
- Document assumptions and call out at least one material sensitivity or risk.

### Constraints
- Stay inside the provided company, history, and driver set unless you explicitly label a side case.
- Do **not** build a DCF, comps, or valuation memo — this is a three-statement forecast work sample.
- Prefer a spreadsheet (LibreOffice Calc / Excel) a reviewer can open; short written notes are fine alongside.
- Talk through your reasoning; opaque scrap numbers without links or checks are weak.

### Deliverables
An auditable workbook (and/or completed `model_template.md`) with linked IS / BS / CF for history checks and the 5-year forecast, plus brief assumption notes. Optional charts are fine; not required.

{{company_name}} — forecast drivers ({{scenario_name}})
================================================================
All figures USD thousands unless noted. Forecast years = FY2025–FY2029 (Y1–Y5).
Base year for the forecast rollforward = FY2024.

Revenue growth (YoY):
  Y1 {{growth_y1}}%, Y2 {{growth_y2}}%, Y3 {{growth_y3}}%, Y4 {{growth_y4}}%, Y5 {{growth_y5}}%

Gross margin (gross profit / revenue):
  Y1 {{gm_y1}}%, Y2 {{gm_y2}}%, Y3 {{gm_y3}}%, Y4 {{gm_y4}}%, Y5 {{gm_y5}}%

Operating expense excluding D&A (% of revenue):
  Y1 {{opex_y1}}%, Y2 {{opex_y2}}%, Y3 {{opex_y3}}%, Y4 {{opex_y4}}%, Y5 {{opex_y5}}%

Tax rate: {{tax_rate_pct}}% of EBT each year

D&A policy:
  D&A_t = {{da_pct}}% × beginning-of-year net PP&E
  Net PP&E_t = beginning net PP&E + CapEx_t − D&A_t

CapEx (% of that year’s revenue):
  Y1 {{capex_pct_y1}}%, Y2 {{capex_pct_y2}}%, Y3 {{capex_pct_y3}}%, Y4 {{capex_pct_y4}}%, Y5 {{capex_pct_y5}}%

Net working capital days (year-end balances):
  DSO (AR): {{dso}} days → AR = revenue × {{dso}} / 365
  DIO (inventory): {{dio}} days → Inventory = COGS × {{dio}} / 365
  DPO (AP): {{dpo}} days → AP = COGS × {{dpo}} / 365

Interest expense (USD thousands):
  Y1 {{int_y1}}, Y2 {{int_y2}}, Y3 {{int_y3}}, Y4 {{int_y4}}, Y5 {{int_y5}}

Debt:
  Repay ${{debt_paydown}}k principal each forecast year (no new draws)

Dividends:
  {{dividend_payout_pct}}% of that year’s net income

Common stock:
  Remains ${{common_stock}}k (no equity issuance)

Cash:
  Plug from the cash flow statement so the balance sheet balances
  Ending cash must equal beginning cash + CFO + CFI + CFF

Do not build a DCF or valuation. Focus on an integrated three-statement forecast.
